subject: Temporary throughput escrow & SLA addendum request — Aurora launch
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@aurorahealth.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@starlens.io>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary throughput escrow and SLA addendum for launch

Hi Jonas —

Quick context: Aurora is running a national push the week of Oct 12 (paid media + partner integrations). We expect a 6‑hour peak window each day where traffic to the inference endpoints will increase ~6x versus baseline. Our engineering team is comfortable with graceful degradation, but this is a customer‑facing experience (claims intake) and we need a tighter latency envelope during the peak.

Specifically, we are asking Redwood for:
- A temporary reserved throughput pool (token escrow) for the launch window: Oct 12–14 local time, daily 14:00–20:00 ET.
- A short SLA addendum that guarantees median p95 latency under 450ms for requests routed to the reserved pool.
- A mutually agreed fallback policy and fair‑use guardrails so other customers are not impacted.

I attached our launch forecast (aurora_launch_forecast.csv) with token/hour estimates. Happy to hop on a call this week — timeline is tight so we need to confirm feasibility and pricing by 2027‑09‑17.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Integrations, Aurora Health
samir@aurorahealth.ai
(415) 555‑0139

[Attachment: aurora_launch_forecast.csv (csv)]

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput escrow and SLA addendum for launch

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Short answer: we can support a short, timeboxed reserved pool and an SLA addendum, but we need to lock down the exact token budget, enforcement knobs, and a billing retainer for reserved capacity.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus — can you validate a reserved pool config that isolates the traffic and enforces p95 target via routing and a small priority token pool? Would like a config by EOD tomorrow so we can run capacity checks.
2) Laura — I will need commercial terms (retainer amount & DocuSign) and a suggested SLA appendix that legal can review.
3) Samir — can you confirm the Oct 12–14 window and the hourly token spike in the attached CSV? Also confirm whether all requests are within a single model endpoint or a mix.

We’ll plan for an operational runbook: 1) dedicated pool routing, 2) prewarming and cache seeding 3) realtime dashboard and an on‑call escalation line. If all parties agree, we can turn this into a 72‑hour appendix (signed) and a short SOW.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput escrow and SLA addendum for launch

Samir / Jonas —

I reviewed the forecast. Feasibility notes: we can create a reserved throughput pool for Oct 12–14 with the following guardrails and controls:

- Reserved pool size: configurable up to 2.4M tokens/day (we recommend starting with 1.8M and scaling if telemetry shows headroom).
- Enforcement: token accounting at routing layer with hard caps per minute and a soft throttling threshold. Soft throttling begins at 85% of the pool with server‑side backpressure and a 10% degraded‑response fallback to a lower‑cost model variant.
- Latency target: with prewarmed workers and cache seeding we can target p95 <= 420ms; p99 will be higher during sustained peak.
- Fairness: we will isolate the reserved pool on dedicated capacity and apply a strict token accounting mechanism; cluster autoscaling will not pull extra capacity from general shared pools during the window (to avoid impact to others).

Attachments: reserved_pool_config.yaml (example config we’d apply).

Operational ask: we need a signed appendix to set the exact pool size and the penalty/rollback if traffic exceeds the reserved pool without notice. Also require a $Xk retainer to reserve the capacity (applied to usage on invoice).

I’ll prepare the config and a short runbook; request a quick tech review with Aurora’s infra lead this week.

—Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

[Attachment: reserved_pool_config.yaml (yaml)]

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@aurorahealth.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput escrow & SLA addendum request — Aurora launch

Samir —

Appreciate the context. From a commercial perspective we can do the 72‑hour reserved pool and SLA appendix. Summary of terms we’ll put in DocuSign: 

- Reserved pool: 1.8M tokens/day (scaling to 2.4M upon mutual signoff) for Oct 12–14, 14:00–20:00 ET each day.
- Retainer: $12,500 to reserve dedicated capacity (applied to final usage invoice).
- SLA addendum: p95 latency target <= 450ms for requests routed to the reserved pool; credits apply only if both parties meet runbook obligations (prewarm, traffic shaping).
- Excess traffic: will be rate‑limited at pool cap; Aurora can opt into burst overflow to shared capacity at pay‑as‑you‑go rates (higher unit price).

I attached a draft appendix (SLA_appendix_v1.pdf) and a DocuSign link for signature. If that looks fine, Jonas and Marcus will coordinate technical readiness and we’ll add the appendix to the master SOW.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

[Attachment: SLA_appendix_v1.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. We accept the 1.8M tokens/day initial pool and the $12,500 retainer. I’ve asked our legal to run the appendix but I don’t expect substantive changes. Please send the DocuSign link and we’ll aim to sign by EOD Monday (2027‑09‑20).

One operational note: can Marcus and team add a short list of telemetry events/thresholds we should watch (error rate, queue depth, median latency) so our on‑call can monitor during the launch window?

Will sign soon — appreciate the quick turnaround.
